description: Resolver: a contact with no visibility group returns ticketScope 'client' and visibleBoardIds null — today's behavior, unchanged.
Resolver: a contact in a group with ticket_scope 'contact' returns effective scope 'contact', and one with 'client' returns 'client'.

Resolver: a contact with is_client_admin true in a 'contact'-scoped group resolves to effective scope 'client' (the override), and the same contact with is_client_admin absent/false resolves to 'contact'.
Resolver: a missing group and a cross-client group each still throw their existing error, preserving fail-closed behavior.

Helper unit: with effective scope 'client' the contact predicate is not applied and the board predicate behaves exactly as applyVisibilityBoardFilter did — including null (no filter) and empty-array (1 = 0) cases. Primary regression guard.
Helper unit: with effective scope 'contact' AND a board list, both predicates are applied together (composition).

Helper unit: the chosen null-contact policy is asserted explicitly — a ticket with contact_name_id NULL is matched or not matched per the decision in OQ1, with the test named so the policy is discoverable.
Enforcement matrix, scope 'contact': a sibling contact's ticket is absent from the portal ticket list, ticket detail, and ticket documents.

Enforcement matrix, scope 'contact': a sibling contact's ticket is excluded from the dashboard open-ticket count and does not appear in the dashboard activity feed (neither title nor comment excerpt).
Direct-ID denial: a contact-scoped user calling resolveVisibleTicket with a sibling's ticket ID is refused, which closes the comment add/update/delete AND status-change paths that sit behind it.
Client-admin override end to end: a contact-scoped group member with is_client_admin true sees sibling tickets on list, detail, and dashboard count.
Default-scope regression: with every group left at 'client', list, detail, documents, dashboard count, and dashboard feed return exactly what they returned before this change.

DB-backed REST: in ticketClientPortalAbac.integration.test.ts, a contact-scoped API subject gets only their own tickets from list, search, count, and getById, with pagination totals consistent; a client-admin subject gets all of the client's.

DB-backed real-SQL guard: each enforcement site's query executes successfully against migrated schema with a board-restricted AND contact-scoped group, proving column/alias correctness. This is the test class that would have caught the 't.board_id'-against-unaliased-'tickets' defect, which mock-level assertions cannot.
DB-backed: the migration applies to a database with existing visibility groups, every pre-existing row reads back ticket_scope 'client', and the CHECK constraint rejects any third value.

Actions round-trip: creating and then updating a group with scope 'contact' persists and reads back through BOTH the portal-side and MSP-side action modules, and an MSP-side update that does not mention scope leaves it intact.
Locale parity: the new client-portal visibility-group keys and the new msp/contacts scope keys exist in all ten locales, with 'pt' now included in the parity assertion.

Portal-side group editor: the scope control renders both options, defaults to 'client' for a new group, hydrates the saved scope when editing an existing one, and submits the chosen scope in the payload. Extends the existing VisibilityGroupsSettings component test.

Kernel parity: the new relationship template's JS matches() and its compiled SQL agree for contact-scoped, admin-override, and null-contact cases, asserted through the existing relationshipSqlParity integration harness.
Fail-closed: a client user whose visibility context fails to resolve is denied rather than widened, preserving the catch-and-deny path in both ticketActions and optimizedTicketActions.

Live-token leak guard: a contact-scoped portal session calling GET /api/tickets/{siblingTicketId}/live-token is refused and no Hocuspocus token is minted — asserted both through getTicketById narrowing and through the route's own user-type rejection.
